notes:
A supply-transport op with a four-way choice of theatre, and the whole reading is about how that choice is expressed. The player picks ONE Bastokan-controlled area and does the whole errand there.

Where the alternatives are NAMED, MARKABLE NPCs I split them into one rung per zone sharing a group, each carrying its own zone and grid: the Gate Sentry at North Gustaberg (S) (F-7), Grauberg (S) (L-5), Pashhow Marshlands (S) (I-11) and Rolanberry Fields (S) (I-14) as group "sentry", and the four differently-named Campaign NPCs -- Jagged Onyx, L.C. (North Gustaberg (S) D-10), Polished Fang, L.C. (Grauberg (S) I-8), Stray Boar, L.C. (Pashhow Marshlands (S) K-6), Wayward Echo, L.C. (Rolanberry Fields (S) J-7) -- as group "deliver". Group members are all current together and all draw, which is exactly what "go to any one of these" wants; only ONE member need actually be done, which a group cannot say, hence both or_branch_modelled and unordered_group. Giving each rung its real zone matters twice over: it stops the row inheriting the giver's Bastok Markets (S) in the where-readout, and "Gate Sentry" is the same name in four places, so without a zone the row is an ambiguous NPC.

The ??? stage is the exception and is deliberately ONE rung with a null zone, the four positions written out verbatim in its note. Splitting it four ways would have put the [KI] Campaign Supplies on four rungs, and duplicated evidence is fatal in stage C -- it would have cost this record its whole ladder to gain zone labels on an object that can never carry a marker anyway. That rung is also optional: bullet 2 says the Gate Sentry EITHER hands you the Campaign Supplies outright OR tells you to go find them, and only the second branch sends you to a ???. Holding the key item is true either way, which is why it sits on that rung.

Grid conflict worth a human's eye: this page puts the Grauberg (S) Gate Sentry at (L-5); BG Wiki's Gate Sentry NPC page (fetched separately, not part of this page) puts it at (L-4). I kept this page's (L-5) because the ladder is this page's reading, and I am naming the other source rather than silently averaging them.

"List of Gate Sentries:", "List of ??? positions:" and "List of Campaign NPCs:" are HEADINGS, not names, and none of them appears in any target. The last two sentences of the page ("Once you've arrived at the Campaign NPC, talk to him/her..." and "After talking to Hieronymus, the mission is complete.") render as trailing lines under bullet 14 rather than as bullets of their own, so the deliver group and the final rung both cite [14]. Bullet 1 ("Easily soloable mission") is advice.

The Gate Sentry may also impose extra conditions -- deliver fast because the cargo will spoil, or avoid all combat because it is fragile. Those are per-run modifiers announced in dialogue, not a header Time limit (Time is empty) and not something the addon can observe, so they are recorded in the step note only. It is recorded as `items` on the photograph rung instead, which is the honest way to say "you must be carrying this".

notes:
Three rungs -- accept, run the fortification-crystal minigame at the arbiter, report back -- and the middle one is unmarkable for a reason worth stating.

The page says "speak to the active Campaign arbiter", which is a ROLE, not a name, and it is not even a wikilink in the source. I looked it up rather than guess: BG Wiki's Campaign Arbiter page is a redirect to Campaign Arbiters, which lists the actual NPCs under individual names -- Saphiriance, T.K.; Arlayse, R.K.; Uriah, C.A.; Jagged Onyx, L.C. and so on -- and explains that "Campaign Arbiters" is a designation, with the nation ones signified by rank suffixes. So there is no in-game entity called "Campaign arbiter", and writing that string into target.name would mint a marker key that can never draw. Target is {"type": "none"} and the detail lives in the step note. That lookup is from the wiki, not from this page.

The zone is null for the same kind of reason: the page says only "a Windurst controlled Campaign area" and "the Fortification tower in the zone" -- it enumerates no zones at all, so there is nothing to record and nothing to split into a group. A null zone matches anywhere, which is the honest answer; it is flagged so the where-readout falling back to the giver's Windurst Waters (S) is not mistaken for a claim.

I looked it up rather than guess: BG Wiki's Campaign Arbiter page is a redirect to Campaign Arbiters, which lists the actual NPCs under individual names -- Saphiriance, T.K.; Arlayse, R.K.; Uriah, C.A.; Jagged Onyx, L.C. and so on -- and explains that "Campaign Arbiters" is a designation, with the nation ones signified by rank suffixes. So there is no in-game entity called "Campaign arbiter", and writing that string into target.name would mint a marker key that can never draw. Target is {"type": "none"} and the detail lives in the step note. That lookup is from the wiki, not from this page.

The zone is null for the same kind of reason: the page says only "a Windurst controlled Campaign area" and "the Fortification tower in the zone" -- it enumerates no zones at all, so there is nothing to record and nothing to split into a group. The Windurst twin of Deep Cover I (B), and the differences are all real ones I read off this page rather than assumed: the op NPC is Pelpopo, not Mariette; the quarry is Yagudos, not Quadavs; bullet 3 says "They will provide" where the (B) page says "She"; and bullet 9, about extra Fiend Plates carrying into Deep Cover II (W), is NOT struck through here whereas the corresponding bullet on Deep Cover I (B) is struck through in the wikitext.
